headline: AI built a 91% win-rate crypto bot after a 217% buy-and-hold reality check
summary: A new AI-driven crypto trading bot achieved a 91% win-rate, but only after a 'buy-and-hold' strategy delivered a 217% return, highlighting the challenge of balancing high gains with significant drawdown risk.
details: After months of building technical indicator bots, a simple 'buy and hold' test on BTC/JPY over eight years yielded a +217.1% return. This benchmark far surpassed all timed entry/exit strategies, which only managed a fraction of that gain.

However, the buy-and-hold approach came with a severe 54.49% maximum drawdown, a risk that would liquidate most retail accounts. The bots, designed to avoid pullbacks, kept drawdowns in the 13-17% range, reframing the goal to capturing upside without extreme wipeout risk.

The AI agent then shifted focus from a single perfect bot to a diversified portfolio, even finding that 'losing' strategies could provide diversification. This counterintuitive reality showed that seemingly 'bad' strategies can act as insurance for 'good' ones within a portfolio.

The agent also explored a market-neutral basis-fade strategy, betting on the price gap between leverage and spot products. During this, it identified critical 'phantom loss' and 'silent zero' bugs, revealing errors in cost accounting and fee attribution.

Crucially, the agent highlighted a structural decay in the strategy's edge, with trade frequency dropping significantly over time. This indicated that the 'edge' was a symptom of early-market volatility, diminishing as the market matured.

Further tests included classic Japanese technical analysis and various timeframes. While weekly trading showed an impressive Profit Factor of 2.74, its extremely low trade count (17 trades in 8 years) rendered it statistically unreliable for practical use.

Ultimately, the AI built and backtested nine distinct candidates, with only two (C3 and C7) surviving all stress tests. The key takeaway is the AI's role as a 'world-class skeptic,' identifying flaws even in high win-rate strategies.

The experiment concludes with a choice between the high-yield/high-pain path of the benchmark or the slower, managed grind of portfolio blends. All code, the backtest engine, and logs of rejected strategies are publicly available on GitHub.

headline: Stop Slouching! Build a Real-Time Spine Posture Monitor using MediaPipe and Python
summary: This tutorial leverages MediaPipe and Python to track your posture via webcam, sending notifications when you slouch. It's ideal for developers interested in computer vision and ergonomics.
details: Long hours at the keyboard often lead to 'tech neck,' a common issue for developers that can hinder productivity. This tutorial addresses the problem by guiding users through building a real-time spine posture monitor.

The project utilizes real-time human pose estimation with MediaPipe and Python libraries. It tracks your posture via a webcam and sends system notifications when slouching is detected, helping maintain proper ergonomics.

The core logic involves capturing video frames and processing them through a pre-trained neural network to identify 33 3D body landmarks. Basic geometry is then applied to determine if your posture is healthy.
To detect slouching, the system measures the angle between the ear and the shoulder. In correct posture, the ear aligns vertically with the shoulder; a forward lean increases this angle.
The webcam feed is continuously monitored, and if a user maintains a bad posture for more than 3 seconds, a system notification is triggered using PyObjC.

While this script is a great weekend project, building production-ready health monitoring tools requires addressing edge cases. These include varying lighting conditions, multi-person detection, and battery optimization.
